For several weeks each fall and winter, schools of migrating mullet can be seen along Florida's Gulf and Atlantic coasts. To capture the scale and majesty of the annual mullet run, National Geographic Explorer Mac Stone dropped into the clear waters south of the Everglades, coming face to face with millions of fish in one of North America's largest marine migrations. Presented by @ROLEX. Pangolins are notoriously difficult to rehabilitate and rewild because they need to learn where to forage for food. During their daily walks, carers at the Tikki Hywood Foundation's rescue center in Cameroon lend a helping hand by pointing infant pangolins to places they can find ants and termites and encouraging them to eat. Presented by @ROLEX. On Mozambique’s Mount Mabu, National Geographic Explorer Gimo Daniel is using an unusual bait to hunt for new dung beetle species: human poop. It’s messy work, but his discoveries could help make the case for protecting the forest.
